title: Choose TwinSleuth’s visual direction
question: The roll assigned a machine fault-isolation schematic. Keep it, choose another direction, or re-roll the hand.

options.label: Fault-Isolation Schematic
options.lineage: Industrial service prints and machine fault-finding sheets
options.thesis: A live service schematic makes the machine and its candidate faults the center of the diagnostic work.
options.viewport: The PIN-9 arm drawing anchors the left; a compact cause register and probe rail sit beside it; the prediction controls occupy a clearly marked right column; observed rows span the sheet below.
options.risk: Callouts can compete with the action if the active probe and prediction column do not own the strongest contrast.

raised.raise: Cause descriptions reveal on selection while the unselected register stays compact.
One oversized case identifier and a single signal field anchor the first view.
The arm diagram keeps the same component scale across states for honest comparison.

options.label: Test-Bench Record
options.lineage: Instrumented laboratory worksheets and experimental run sheets
options.thesis: A single test record puts the learner’s prediction beside the result that will challenge it.
options.viewport: A large run title opens the sheet; a four-row cause matrix sits beside the machine state; the chosen probe and prediction column are the strongest block; evidence appends as new rows beneath.
options.risk: A table-first layout can underplay the simulated machine if the drawing becomes a thumbnail.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: A vertical score gives the diagnostic episode a precise, readable order in time.
options.viewport: A tall central score follows prediction, probe, and result as a staff; the arm and current input stay in a side column.
options.risk: The dance vocabulary could make an industrial training tool feel unfamiliar.
options.case: Strong sequence clarity, weaker maintenance identity; the vertical staff stays an alternate because test order matters.

options.label: Constructed Grid
options.thesis: A visible construction grid makes every forecast and evidence row feel measured and deliberate.
options.viewport: The case identifier is built from oversized grid geometry; the working table and cause list snap to the same cells.
options.risk: The specimen’s formal grid could become the subject instead of the diagnosis.
options.case: Strong product clarity through a strict measurement grid, weaker workshop identity; it remains a full alternate.

options.label: Concourse State Board
options.thesis: A ruled status board makes every state change public, immediate, and easy to scan.
options.viewport: The current case state occupies the board header; each probe and result becomes a row with one stable status column.
options.risk: A board of statuses alone cannot carry the learner’s evidence argument.
options.case: State-change clarity is strong and familiar in operations, but the board must yield space to reasoning; kept as an alternate.

options.label: Streaming Catalog Wall
options.lineage: Streaming catalogs and expanding poster rails
options.thesis: The causes become a wall of browsable tiles, with the focused fault expanding to show its details.
options.viewport: Large cause tiles form horizontal rails; the selected cause expands and the others recede.
options.risk: A browsing metaphor makes the diagnostic job feel optional and exploratory.
options.case: Both audience identification and product clarity lose to the roll: learners test causes rather than browse a catalog.
options.kept: Focused cause selection reveals its description without expanding every row.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.thesis: The active diagnostic step floods the screen with one color while oversized words carry navigation.
options.viewport: A panoramic sequence of color fields carries the case name, current test, and next action.
options.risk: Panorama and cropped language would compete with dense evidence and four prediction controls.
options.case: Both audience identification and task clarity lose: the diagnostic work needs steady comparison, not a sliding panorama.
options.kept: One large case identifier and a single high-contrast active field establish focus.

options.label: Botanical Sequence Folio
options.lineage: Registered botanical plates across a plant’s life cycle
options.thesis: Each probe is a fixed-scale plate in an illustrated progression from symptom to diagnosis.
options.viewport: A series of machine states sits on one baseline, with a caption under each probe.
options.risk: A life-cycle metaphor suggests natural stages that the fault case does not have.
options.case: Both axes lose: a plant’s stages do not map to competing faults or the learner’s test decisions.
options.kept: The machine diagram holds one consistent scale so changes remain comparable.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional operations dashboard with a navigation rail and separate forecast, activity, and result panels.
canonCard.viewport: A left navigation rail frames a centered dashboard; each task stage lives in its own panel.
canonCard.risk: Familiar structure makes the task legible but does little to make prediction-before-evidence memorable.
